'''Erwin Louis Hahn''' (June 9, 1921 – September 20, 2016) was an American [[physicist]], best known for his work on [[nuclear magnetic resonance]] (NMR).<ref name="Filler2009b">Filler, AG: The history, development, and impact of computed imaging in neurological diagnosis and neurosurgery: CT, MRI, DTI: [http://precedings.nature.com/documents/3267/version/4 Nature Precedings ] {{doi|10.1038/npre.2009.3267.4}}.</ref> In 1950 he discovered the [[spin echo]].<ref name=hahn>{{cite journal| author = Hahn, E.L.| title = Spin echoes| journal = Physical Review| date = 1950| volume = 80| issue = 4| pages = 580–594| doi = 10.1103/PhysRev.80.580|bibcode = 1950PhRv...80..580H }}</ref>

== Biography ==

=== Education ===
He grew up in  [[Sewickley, Pennsylvania]]. He received his [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] in Physics from [[Juniata College]] and his [[Master of Science|M.S.]] and [[Doctor of Philosophy]] from the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]]. He served as an enlisted sailor in the [[United States Navy]] and was an instructor on radar and sonar.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Pines|first1=Alexander|last2=Budker|first2=Dmitry|date=2019-12-01|title=Erwin Louis Hahn. 9 June 1921—20 September 2016|journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society|volume=68|pages=219–230|doi=10.1098/rsbm.2019.0038|doi-access=free}}</ref>

=== Career and research ===
He was professor of physics, from 1955 to 1991, and subsequently, [[Professor Emeritus]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name="AAAS">{{cite web|title=Book of Members, 1780–2010: Chapter H|url=http://www.amacad.org/publications/BookofMembers/ChapterH.pdf|publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences|access-date=September 22, 2016}}</ref> 

He died at the age of 95 in 2016.<ref name="Rem Berkeley">{{cite web|title=Remembering Erwin Hahn|url=http://physics.berkeley.edu/news-events/news/20160922/remembering-erwin-hahn|website=Physics @ Berkeley|access-date=September 23, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160924021303/http://physics.berkeley.edu/news-events/news/20160922/remembering-erwin-hahn|archive-date=September 24, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Research ==
Hahn discovered experimentally and popularized the concept of [[spin echo]] in 1950.<ref name="hahn" />

Hahn and his PhD student {{Ill|Sven R. Hartmann|de}} developed the [[cross-polarization]] technique in 1961.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-06-22 |title=Sven Hartmann {{!}} Department of Physics |url=https://www.physics.columbia.edu/news/sven-hartmann |access-date=2026-07-01 |website=www.physics.columbia.edu |language=en}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
Hahn was elected a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1971.<ref name="AAAS" />

In 1993 he was awarded the [[Comstock Prize in Physics]] from the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="Comstock">{{cite web|title=Comstock Prize in Physics |url=http://www.nasonline.org/site/PageServer?pagename=AWARDS_comstock |publisher=National Academy of Sciences |access-date=13 February 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101229195326/http://www.nasonline.org/site/PageServer?pagename=AWARDS_comstock |archive-date=29 December 2010 }}</ref> In 2013, Sir [[Peter Mansfield]] said in his autobiography that Hahn was "the person who really missed out" the [[Nobel Prize]] for his contribution to the principles of spin echoes.<ref name="Mansfield217">{{cite book|author=Peter Mansfield |year=2013 |page=217 |title=The long road to Stockholm. The story of MRI. An autobiography|publisher=OUP Oxford |isbn=978-0-19-966454-2}}</ref>

He also received the 2016 Gold Medal from the [[International Society for Magnetic Resonance in Medicine]] (ISMRM). The award, ISMRM's highest honor, was given to Hahn for his creation of pulsed magnetic resonance and processes of signal refocusing which are essential to modern day MRI.<ref name="Gold Medal Award">{{cite web|title=Erwin Hahn Receives Gold Medal Award|url=http://physics.berkeley.edu/news-events/news/20160630/erwin-hahn-receives-gold-medal-award|website=Physics @ Berkeley|access-date=September 29, 2016|archive-date=October 2, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161002095714/http://physics.berkeley.edu/news-events/news/20160630/erwin-hahn-receives-gold-medal-award|url-status=dead}}</ref>
